full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted the suit against opposite party No. 1 The opposite party No. 2 on his own representation was added as defendant No. 2 in the said suit and others were impleaded as proforma-defendants by the plaintiff. The suit was for declaration of title in the land in suit on the ground that ROR Khatian was erroneously recorded in the name of the Government of Bangladesh, opposite party No. 1. The case of the plaintiff was, in short, that land in suit originally belonged to Zaminder Brajendra Kishore Roy Chowdhury from whom plaintiffs father Jaha Box Bepari took jote pattan an 25th Bhadra, 1351 BS at a rental of Taka 6.00 on payment of najar selami. He got possession of the same on assertion of his title to the knowledge of all. Jaha Box died leaving plaintiff-petitioner as a son and proforma defendant Nos. 3-8 as other heirs. On amicable arrangement with the other heirs of Jaha Box the plaintiff alone got the land in suit and was in exclusive possession therein. His further case was that in the middle part of Falgoon, 1387 BS he learnt for the first time the wrong recording of the land in suit in the name of the Government. Hence the suit. 

 3. The opposite party-Government and added defendant No. 2(opposite party No. 2) resisted the suit by filing two sets of written statement, The case of the opposite party No. 1 was that the erstwhile Government of Pakistan acquired the suit jote from the ex-landlord Brajendra Kishore Roy Chowdhury and paid adequate compensation for the same to the ex-landlord. The ROR Khatian, according to opposite party No.1, correctly stood in the name of the Government. The case of the opposite party No. 2 (Defendant No. 2) is for easement right upon the land in suit on the plea that he purchased adjacent land of plot No. 923 in 1977. 

 The trial Court on consideration of evidence on record held that ROR Khatian No. 1 was wrongly recorded and upon such finding he decreed the suit declaring that the plaintiff has got title in the suit land. 

 5. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that admittedly the suit land appertaining to CS Plot No. 494 is 04 acres out of 3.36 acres which was recorded in CS Khatian as kandi land and not as chandina land and the plaintiffs father having had taken settlement of the land in 1351 BS (September, 1944) the settlement is governed by the Bengal Tenancy Act and not by the Transfer of Property Act. The lower appellate Court erred in holding that the land is chandina land and that the plaintiff failed to produce bilateral deed and that the settlement with regard to the suit land was not valid in law. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali submitted that when settlement is made by the Zaminder in respect of an agricultural land governed by Bengal Tenancy Act, no document in writing is necessary for making such settlement and accordingly the learned Court of appeal below committed mistake in law leading to mistake in his decision and that has occasioned failure of justice.
